usage.title: Cloudflare Free plan usage
usage.intro: How much of the free Cloudflare allowances was used today, whether the next game fits, and what different plans would cost. Every number below is one of three kinds; do not mix them up.
usage.kind.estimate.help: A forecast from the application's model. Not a measurement and not a Cloudflare bill.
usage.kind.measured.help: Counters the application keeps about itself. A lower bound: Cloudflare sees more (page and API requests are not counted one by one).
usage.kind.official.help: Figures from the Cloudflare dashboard that you type in yourself. Only these are official.
usage.limitsDate: Limits come from config/cloudflare-limits.json, last verified
usage.noAlerts: No resource has reached a threshold today.
usage.measuredNote: "Measured" covers finished games and image uploads; a game that is still running is added when it ends. For safety compare with the Cloudflare dashboard and enter its figures below: alerts use the larger of the two.
usage.cpuNote: CPU time per invocation (10 ms) is not measured by the application: it is a per-call limit, not a daily sum. Check it on a real Cloudflare account under load.
usage.off.title: Official figures from the Cloudflare dashboard
usage.off.help: Open the Cloudflare dashboard → Workers & Pages → your app → Metrics (Durable Objects and D1 have their own sections), find the day's value and type it here. No API token is needed.
usage.off.badValue: Enter a number, zero or more.
usage.calc.title: Calculator
usage.calc.help: Enter the expected use to see what it needs and how much of the free allowance remains. "Worst case": 120 participants, at least 50 questions and 90 minutes, three reconnects per participant, 3 messages per question.
usage.calc.bottleneck: The resource that runs out first
usage.calc.gamesPerDay: games of this size per day
usage.calc.note: A model built on local measurements; not yet checked on a real Cloudflare account. Limits are daily; "per month" is for reference. Storage accumulates over the retention period.
usage.th.title: Alert thresholds
usage.th.help: The percentage of the daily limit at which each level appears. The "quota reached" level (100 %) is fixed.
usage.pre.title: A Cloudflare limit is close
usage.pre.intro: By estimate, this game would push these resources toward their daily limit. Cloudflare does not charge: once a limit is used up, operations simply stop working until 00:00 UTC.
usage.pre.fit: More games like this that fit today
usage.pre.safeHelp: At most {n} participants and no extras. This lowers the load but does not remove the limit.
usage.pre.noPaid: No paid Cloudflare features are switched on and the plan is not changed.
err.invalid_thresholds: Thresholds must rise: whole numbers from 1 to 99 %.

upd.title: Gart updates
upd.intro: New versions come from the project's public releases on GitHub. The digital signature is checked before anything is installed: a package changed after release is never installed. Your quizzes, results and administrators are not changed.
upd.connectP: To update the site, Gart needs your Cloudflare token. It is stored encrypted and is available only to this site; you can delete it at any time.
upd.s3: Add permissions: Account → Workers Scripts → Edit; Account → D1 → Edit; Account → Account Settings → Read.
upd.s4: Under “Account Resources” pick your account, create the token and paste it below.
upd.workerHint: Shown in Cloudflare → Workers & Pages. For an address like name.account.workers.dev it is the first part.
upd.rollbackH: Go back to an earlier version
upd.rollbackP: Installs the selected earlier release. Database changes are not undone: they add to the data rather than remove it, so the earlier version works with them.
upd.running: Working… Keep this page open. The site may briefly stop answering while it switches over.
upd.failed: It did not work. The site stays on the previous version unless the “Server code” step had already finished.
upd.confirmH: Attention: this update changes or removes data in the database
upd.confirmP: Migrations: {list}. It is wise to take a backup first (the backup section of the guide).
upd.ownerOnly: This tab is for the owner.
listen.title: Gart music and sounds
listen.intro: The music was written for Gart and is played in your browser: nothing is downloaded from the internet. Pick a variant and a mood. All three use the “Ukrainian Dorian” scale (a minor scale with a raised fourth).
listen.about.sopilka: Calm and songlike: flute, dulcimer arpeggios and a quiet drone.
listen.about.tsymbaly: Light and danceable: the dulcimer carries the tune.
listen.about.hopak: Energetic with a beat: flute, “oom-pah” bass, drum and shaker.

imp.title: Import quizzes from a file
imp.intro: Upload quiz files in the gart.json format: up to {n} files at a time, one quiz per file. Quizzes appear as drafts: review them and activate. Handy for making quizzes with an AI assistant from the template.
imp.show: Show the template with comments for AI
imp.aiHint: Send this file to an AI assistant and ask: “Write a quiz about … in this format”. The comments on keys that start with an underscore (_) are instructions for the AI and are ignored on import.
imp.tooBig: The file is too big (over 512 KB).
imp.notJson: This is not valid JSON. Check that the AI did not add extra text or Markdown.
imp.tooMany: Too many files chosen: importing the first {n}.
imp.p.exactly_one_correct: there must be exactly one correct answer
imp.p.truefalse_needs_two: type truefalse needs exactly two answers
imp.p.invalid_literal: must be exactly this value (format: gart.quiz, version: 1)
imp.p.too_small: too short or too few items
imp.p.too_big: too long or too many items
imp.p.invalid_enum_value: not one of the allowed values

set.defaultTimeLimitSec.help: How many seconds players have if the question has no time of its own. A question with its own time (shown in the question list) ignores this value. Works only while the time limit is on.
set.timerEnabled.help: On: every question has a timer. The time comes from "Default time per question" (now {n} s), or from the question itself if it has its own. Off: no timer, the host closes each question, and there is no speed bonus.
set.basePoints.help: Points for a correct answer before any bonus. If a question has its own points, they replace this value.
set.speedBonusPercent.help: Extra points for speed, up to {n}% of the base points. An instant answer earns the full bonus, an answer at the very end earns none. Example: 1000 base points and 20% give the fastest player up to 200 extra. No time limit, no bonus.
set.countdownBeforeQuestionSec.help: A pause before each question so players can get ready. Default {n} s; 0 means no countdown.
set.randomizeQuestions.help: Every game shows the questions in a new random order.
set.randomizeAnswers.help: The answers appear in a different order each time, so the right one is not always in the same place. True/False questions are not shuffled.
set.leaderboardEnabled.help: After each question except the last, the host can show the ranking table. After the last question the winners are shown straight away.
set.showCorrectAnswer.help: When a question closes, the screen shows which answer was right.
set.showExplanations.help: After the question, its explanation is shown if the question has one.
set.showFinalLeaderboard.help: At the end of the game a summary with the winners' podium is shown.
set.allowLateJoin.help: Players can join with the PIN or QR code after the game has started: they see the current question and score on the ones they manage to answer. Off: the door is closed after the start.
set.autoAdvance.help: The game moves on by itself without the host pressing anything: {n} s after a question's results and after the ranking table.
set.closeWhenAllAnswered.help: The question closes early as soon as every player who is online has answered. Off: wait for the timer or for the host.
q.overrides: A question's own time or points replace the quiz settings.
imp.overrides: Questions with their own time or points: {n} (they replace the quiz settings)
